result.title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons---a statistical look at the METR plot
result.summary: METR's 50\% time horizon measures the human completion time of software tasks that an AI solves with 50\% probability, allowing AI capabilities to be expressed in interpretable units. On 228 tasks and 26 AIs, we recompute the time horizons using splines and item-response theory to relax the assumption that the AI difficulty of a task depends linearly on the log of human time. Our fitted spline can be interpreted as a function that \emph{converts} human time to AI difficulty; it is nearly flat in a region from 2--30 min but close to linear elsewhere. Hence, a time-horizon jump from 3 min to 30 min is much easier than one from 30 min to 5 hours despite the same multiplier of $10 \times$. Overall, we contribute time-horizon point estimates that perform better under a cross-validated suite of proper scoring rules, as well as diagnostic plots for assessing time horizons' construct validity. We suggest that time horizons be interpreted together with the diagnostic plots, especially as new time-horizon-based benchmarks are proposed or existing ones grow to include longer tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 该文用样条和项目反应理论重算 METR 的 50% 时间视野指标，发现人类完成时间与 AI 难度之间并非对数线性关系，并提供评估该指标构造效度的诊断图。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「人类时间→AI 难度」的非线性转换与构造效度诊断，可能可供核查 LVR 中思考长度、计算成本与收益的度量方式及长度泛化指标设计，但联系较远，需人工判断。
